items.title: Some players hit game-breaking crashes on PS5 and Xbox
items.summary: Dexerto rounds up player reports of repeated crashes since launch — PS5 error CE-108255-1 blocking one player at the early Pipework mission and a PS5 Pro owner in the prologue, plus Xbox Series X crashes minutes into play — with cache clears, database rebuilds and reinstalls not fixing it, and no patch out yet.

items.title: Day-one sales estimate climbs to 24.6 million copies and $2.36 billion
items.summary: Sensor Tower's Thursday-evening update lifts its launch-day estimate to about 24.58 million copies and $2.36 billion, up from 19.1 million and $1.84 billion that morning, with roughly three-quarters of sales on PlayStation; Rockstar and Take-Two still have not confirmed any official figure.

items.title: GTA VI tops an estimated 19.1 million copies and $1.84 billion by launch morning
items.summary: Sensor Tower puts launch-morning sales at about 19.1 million copies and $1.84 billion, more than double GTA V's first-day $815.7 million, though Take-Two has not confirmed any official figure yet; analysts expect roughly $3 billion in sales by the end of the year.

items.title: GTA VI smashes the livestream record with 7.91 million peak viewers
items.summary: Streams Charts counts a 7.91 million peak across Twitch, YouTube and Kick in the first 24 hours, more than four times the old game-launch record, plus 125.47 million hours watched; IShowSpeed was the most-watched creator at 4.47 million hours.

items.title: IGN's Chapter 1 walkthrough maps all 23 opening missions
items.summary: IGN's launch-day walkthrough covers every Chapter 1 mission from the prologue through the Leonida Keys, with early-game tips on money, vehicles, wanted levels and missables to grab before the chapter's points of no return.

items.title: Rockstar confirms GTA VI is now available worldwide
items.summary: Rockstar's launch-day announcement confirms GTA VI is out now for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at the PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, Rockstar Games Store and retailers, calling it the highest-rated game of all time and quoting Sam Houser on a game meant to exceed expectations; the 34-track official album from Atlantic Records lands at midnight.

items.title: GTA VI is already chasing world records on launch day
items.summary: Guinness World Records notes the reveal trailer's 24-hour viewing record and an estimated $750 million in pre-orders two weeks ago, and says a 99 Metacritic average would take the most critically acclaimed game ever from Ocarina of Time, a record held since 1997.

items.title: International critics rave as GTA VI draws 2.3 million Twitch viewers
items.summary: Le Monde rounds up glowing verdicts from IGN, Bloomberg, The Washington Post and the French press, with the first reviews landing at 99 on Metacritic, and reports nearly 2.3 million people were watching GTA VI streams on Twitch by midday Paris time as early players went live from New Zealand.

items.title: Launch day in America: GTA VI is live, and the live blog is rolling
items.summary: USA Today's launch-day live coverage follows the US unlock seconds after midnight ET on November 19, with Sensor Tower estimating $1.65 billion in presales from 17.07 million copies (74% on PS5), first-hour impressions from Vice City, and launch-week food deals including Popeyes' Spice City Sandwich and Subway's Vice City Cubano running through November 22.

items.title: Polygon's cheat guide: GTA VI's cheats stay locked until you beat the story
items.summary: Polygon's launch-day guide explains that a Cheats menu only appears in the Progression tab after you finish the campaign, each cheat sits behind its own unlock condition (with progress made before the credits counting), codes are entered on the phone by holding L1 and R1 and tapping a D-pad sequence, and turning one on disables saving and achievements for the rest of that session.

items.title: 'Grand Theft Callout': nearly one in five US workers plan to take launch day off
items.summary: MarketWatch reports BambooHR data showing 18% of American workers plan to take November 19 off to play GTA VI, with paid-time-off requests running 13% higher than on comparable days, while Logitech is giving staff its first company-wide 'Game Day' and car-buying platform Delivrd is giving employees Friday off to enjoy the launch.

items.title: Won't start on PS5? A required system update is the first fix to check
items.summary: Men's Journal walks through PlayStation's required PS5 system software update 26.07-14.23.00, which Sony says must be installed before GTA VI will play, plus checking for game update 01.002.001 (about 602 MB), confirming up to 212 GB of free space, and what to try if PlayStation Network sign-in fails.

items.title: PlayStation Network buckles under GTA VI launch-eve demand
items.summary: Polygon reports PS5 players ran into login failures, 'services are busy' messages and stalled downloads on November 18 as the pre-load and update rush hit Sony's servers, with Downdetector logging a sharp spike in outage reports even while Sony's own status page listed the network as healthy.

items.title: Push Square's spoiler-free tips: accessibility toggles, classic controls and $100 fast travel
items.summary: Push Square's 12-tip guide covers turning on Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage in Settings, switching back to the Classic GTA 5 control scheme, skipping a RydeMe ride for $100 to fast travel, banking wallet cash at BuckMe ATMs so it is not lost when busted or wasted, and registering a stolen car at Pay 'N' Spray to keep it for good.

items.title: Rockstar leaves sex workers out of GTA VI for the first time in 25 years
items.summary: Consequence reports Rockstar told Shacknews the feature was left out to keep the focus on Jason and Lucia's couple-on-the-run story, carrying forward systems like the wanted system, radio, robberies and car theft instead; strip clubs are still in the game.
